gap: No result ChatGPT got states that macOS has no sharp in-between scaling on a 16-inch 2560x1600 panel: Parkablogs' Teoh Yi Chie found Mac users need the BetterDisplay app for sharp UI scaling on exactly this panel class, while Windows scales it cleanly.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac, PCWorld's best portable monitors and rottenwifi's MacBook list, all opened 2026-11-26. Macworld never mentions scaling or HiDPI and gives no port wattage. PCWorld names DisplayPort Alt Mode in its FAQ but has nothing on macOS scaling or bus power. rottenwifi says to 'check whether the monitor exposes useful HiDPI modes' and calls 2560x1600 a 'practical middle ground', without saying what macOS does at that resolution. ChatGPT's own answer covers part of it (4K gives clean 2x scaling), which is why this is a 2 and not a 3. RTINGS returned only navigation and TechRadar was cut off after its first pick, so those two are unchecked.
decides: It does not reorder the 2560x1600 120 Hz rows, because every row in the line shares the same panel class and the same macOS behaviour. It does qualify the page's premise: the 'matching' panel matches the MacBook's shape and refresh rate, not its text sharpness, and each row needs that caveat with the BetterDisplay workaround named. A shopper who wants Retina-like text at a middle UI size should be pointed to a 4K panel outside the line. The electrical side confirms the plan works: every 16-inch MacBook Pro has Pro or Max silicon that drives at least three external displays natively, so no display driver is needed for one added screen. Intel's 15 W accessory minimum for Thunderbolt 4 and 5 ports is above the 12 W rated power Parkablogs lists for the UPERFECT C2.

findings.label: macOS UI scaling on a 16-inch 2560x1600 portable monitor (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie)
findings.value: "MacOS users will need an app called BetterDisplay for proper (sharp) UI scaling"; "MacOS does not work well with QHD & QHD+ resolution on a 16-inch display." Windows: "sharp visuals regardless of the UI scaling options used."
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Hands-on review of the UPERFECT UPlays C2, a 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz panel. It dates from 2023; I found no 2026 retest on current macOS. I did not verify that the UPlays C2 is the same unit as today's GR16DQ / UGame C2.

findings.label: Why in-between sizes are not sharp at 2560x1600 (BetterDisplay's own guide)
findings.value: "At the same logical desktop size, LoDPI uses one rendering pixel per point along each axis. HiDPI uses two." "On a 2560 × 1440 QHD panel, a 1920 × 1080 HiDPI desktop renders at 3840 × 2160 and is reduced to the panel's grid." "Enabling HiDPI does not turn a low-density panel into a Retina panel."
findings.source_title: How does macOS scaling work, and what are HiDPI and LoDPI? · BetterDisplay Guide
findings.note: My arithmetic for the 16:10 case: clean 2x HiDPI on 2560x1600 gives a 'looks like 1280x800' desktop, and a 'looks like 1920x1200' HiDPI desktop needs a 3840x2400 render reduced to 2560x1600. The guide does not cover 2560x1600 or Apple silicon specifically, and warns "A requested size is not a guaranteed available mode."

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro built-in display versus a 16-inch 2560x1600 panel
findings.value: MacBook: 16.2-inch, 3456-by-2234 at 254 pixels per inch, ProMotion up to 120Hz (Apple). A 16.0-inch 2560x1600 panel works out to about 189 ppi.
findings.note: The 189 ppi is my arithmetic: sqrt(2560² + 1600²) = 3019 px across a 16.0-inch diagonal. That is about 74% of the MacBook's linear pixel density.

findings.label: External displays the current 16-inch MacBook Pro drives natively
findings.value: M5 Pro: "up to three external displays over any combination of Thunderbolt and HDMI ports: three displays up to a native resolution of 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 144Hz". M5 Max: up to four. "Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports support native DisplayPort 2.1 speeds".
findings.note: The 16-inch is sold only with M5 Pro or M5 Max, so the one-external-display limit of base M1/M2/M3 chips does not apply to it. A 2560x1600 panel at 120 or 144 Hz sits below Apple's 4K at 144 Hz ceiling, so the Mac is not the limit on refresh rate.

findings.label: M5 Max MacBook Pro: lid and hub rules for external displays
findings.value: "MacBook Pro models with the M5 Max chip support up to four external displays simultaneously with the built-in display." Closing the lid "will not increase the number of external displays".
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Pro with M5 Max chip - Apple Support (published 2026-11-05)
findings.note: The page does not name screen sizes. It lists up to 4K at 240Hz for a single external display over Thunderbolt or HDMI.

findings.label: Power a Thunderbolt port must supply to a bus-powered accessory (Intel)
findings.value: "Minimum PC port power for accessories": Thunderbolt 5 15W, Thunderbolt 4 15W, USB4 7.5W
findings.source_title: Thunderbolt™ Technology: A Universe of Possibilities (Intel)
findings.note: Intel's Thunderbolt 4 page (https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/architecture-and-technology/thunderbolt/thunderbolt-4-vs-usb-c.html) also reads "up to 15W for computer-powered accessories". This is Intel's certification minimum, not an Apple figure for the MacBook's ports.

findings.label: Single-cable bus power in a named review
findings.value: Rated power listed as 12W; "If your computer can power the display with USB-C, you can use a single cable connection." An LG Gram Style 2023 "is able to power the UPERFECT display to 100% brightness"; "the external display will drain the laptop battery much faster."
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: 12 W rated against the 15 W Thunderbolt minimum leaves 3 W of headroom (my arithmetic). The test laptop was an LG Gram, not a MacBook. Over HDMI the monitor needs a second USB-C cable to a power source.

findings.label: Pass-through charging and measured brightness (Parkablogs)
findings.value: "The power delivery or pass-through charging is less than 10W so can't really charge a laptop through the display." Measured maximum 238 nits against 400 nits advertised; 720 g.
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: This is the 2023 unit. Treat it as a named-reviewer check on listing claims for this panel family, not as a measurement of the current GR16DQ or GR16EQ. The 16-inch MacBook Pro ships with a 140W USB-C Power Adapter (Apple specs page, read 2026-11-26), so the laptop should be charged directly rather than through the monitor.

findings.label: What Macworld's Mac roundup states about it
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 (Macworld, dated 2026-11-25)
findings.note: Macworld gives no power draw, no macOS scaling note and no 120 Hz-on-Mac test. 65 W is under half the 140 W adapter Apple ships with the 16-inch (my arithmetic: 65 / 140 = 46%). Mobile Pixels' own page could not be opened today, so this is the reviewer's figure.

unsourced: Maker power figures for the UPERFECT GR16EQ and GR16DQ, the Duex Float 2 Pro and the SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2: uperfect.com, mobilepixels.us and sotsu.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, through both storecheck.py and direct fetch. The desk-note figures (12 W, 11 W, 65 W pass-through) and all four store prices were therefore not re-read by me.

An Apple-published wattage for what a 16-inch MacBook Pro's Thunderbolt port supplies to a bus-powered device: Apple's current guide pages give no figure, and the 15 W / 7.5 W Apple numbers that turned up in search are from 2016 Intel models. Only Intel's certification minimum is sourced.
A named reviewer's test of 120 Hz or 144 Hz from a MacBook Pro over USB-C on any candidate: Parkablogs describes enabling 120 Hz only in Windows, and Macworld lists 120 Hz as a spec.

An Apple statement of which scaled resolutions macOS offers on a 2560x1600 external display: looked on Apple's display-support pages and found none. The scaling finding rests on Parkablogs and the BetterDisplay guide.
A measured power draw from a MacBook for any candidate (USB-C meter reading by a named reviewer): searched and found none.

Apple's MagSafe 3 line for the 16-inch MacBook Pro (charging separately from the Thunderbolt ports): my read of the specs page returned only the 140W adapter and the three Thunderbolt 5 ports, so MagSafe is left out.
Whether the 2023 UPlays C2 that Parkablogs tested is the same hardware as today's GR16DQ / UGame C2: looked for a maker statement and could not open the store.
RTINGS' portable monitor picks and TechRadar's list beyond its first pick: the pages did not return their article bodies, so I could not check them for this finding.
